__
 
• **Gallium is one of the metals used in LED semiconductor technology**__.

 __
 
• A light-emitting diode (LED) is a semiconductor light source that emits light when current is passed through it.
 
• Gallium is the first and primary element used in the manufacture of almost all semiconductor LED devices.
 
• Gallium is a metallic material found as a trace element in coal, bauxite and other minerals.

• Aluminum gallium arsenide (AlGaAs): red and infrared LEDs

questions.question: Ozone is a molecule made up of ______ oxygen atoms.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**three.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ozone is a molecule composed of three atoms of oxygen, also referred to as O₃**.
 
• A layer of** ozone is present in the stratosphere of Earth and prevents the UV rays from reaching the Earth's surface.**
 
• It is an** allotrope of Oxygen.**
 
• Ozone, or tri-oxygen, is an inorganic molecule with the **chemical formula O₃.**
 
• **It is a pale blue gas with a distinctively pungent smell.**
 
• Ozone is an excellent oxidizing agent as it breaks down into oxygen gas and nascent oxygen. { O₃ → O₂ + [O] }.
 
• It is** an allotrope of oxygen that is much less stable than the diatomic allotrope O2,** breaking down in the lower atmosphere to O2 or di-oxygen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The upper stratosphere consists of a considerable amount of ozone (O3), which protects us from the harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation coming from the sun.
 
• These radiations cause **skin cancer (melanoma)** in humans.
 
• Therefore, **it is important to maintain the ozone shield.**
 
• Ozone in the stratosphere is a product of UV radiations acting on dioxygen (O2) molecules.
 
• The UV radiations split apart molecular oxygen into free oxygen (O) atoms.
 
• These oxygen atoms combine with molecular oxygen to form ozone.

questions.question: Dry ice, ammonium chloride, naphthalene balls, and camphor, all these compounds are an example of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sublimable substances.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sublimation is the process in which a solid substance directly converts into its gaseous form without going through the liquid phase.**
 
• **Dry ice, ammonium chloride, naphthalene balls, and camphor exhibit sublimation on heating. **
 
• Dry ice is solid carbon dioxide, which sublimates at -78.5 degrees Celsius and is commonly used as a cooling agent because it undergoes sublimation, transitioning directly from solid to gas without becoming liquid. This property makes it useful for keeping things cold without leaving behind liquid residue. So while it's not a traditional "cooling agent " like ice packs, it functions effectively in cooling applications due to its sublimation process.
 
• Ammonium chloride, naphthalene balls, and camphor are also sublimable substances that are used for various purposes such as in moth repellents, decongestants, and medicinal ointments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cooling agents are substances that are used to lower the temperature of a system, and all the given compounds can act as cooling agents due to their sublimation properties.**
 
• Inflammable substances are those that can easily catch fire and burn, while solidifying agents are substances that can convert liquids into solids.
 
• None of the given compounds fall under these categories.
 
• Dry ice is commonly used in the transportation of perishable goods as it can maintain a low temperature for an extended period.
 
• Ammonium chloride is used as a flux in the soldering of metals and in the production of dry batteries.
 
• **Naphthalene balls are used as a moth repellent and to prevent musty odors in closets and storage spaces.**
 
• Camphor is used in medicinal ointments and as a flavoring agent in food and beverages.

questions.question: Which of the following gases is referred to as ‘laughing gas’ ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nitrous Oxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Nitrous oxide** is a colorless and odorless substance that's also known as “**laughing gas**.”
 
• It is an oxide of nitrogen with the formula **N₂O**.
 
• When inhaled, the gas slows down the body's reaction time. This results in a calm, euphoric feeling. Nitrous** **oxide can be used to treat pain.
 
• It also functions as a mild sedative. Because of this, it’s sometimes used before dental procedures to promote relaxation and reduce anxiety.
 
• **Side Effects**:
 
 
• Some people also experience hallucinations or sound distortion after inhaling nitrous oxide.
 
• Toxic exposure may lead to a **V****itamin B-12** deficiency or anemia.

questions.question: Which of the following is the allotropic form of carbon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __Graphite__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Graphite is the allotropic form of carbon.**
 
• Graphite, archaically referred to** as plumbago, **is a crystalline form of the element carbon with its atoms arranged in a hexagonal structure. 
 
• There are various allotropes of carbon:
 
 
• **diamond, graphite, lonsdaleite, fullerene, C-540, C-70, amorphous carbon, carbon nanotube**.
 
 
 
• **Diamond and crystalline silicon are isomorphous** because they both have a **three-dimensional tetrahedral structure.**
 
• Allotropy, the existence of **a chemical element in two or more forms, which may differ in the arrangement of atoms in crystalline solids** or in the occurrence of molecules that contain different numbers of atoms.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Coal :**

 
 
• Coal is **a form of amorphous carbon, which is formed by pyrolysis**.

 
 
• **It is an impure form of carbon. **
 
 
 
 
 
• Charcoal is also an allotrope of carbon that is formed by the process of pyrolysis.
 
• **Diamond :**
 
 
• Diamond and fullerene are **pure forms of carbon.**
 
• Diamond is** a solid form of the element carbon with its atoms arranged in a crystal structure called diamond cubic.**
 
 
 
• **Lamp Black :**
 
 
• Lampblack is **a simple genuine pigment made of carbon black.**
 
• The pure carbon pigment is made from the residual soot from burning oil and its name comes from the practice of making it with oil lamps.
 
• Older and less stable blacks made from oil also existed and were called oil black or flame black.

questions.question: Which is a slow cooking process that begins around 320°F, removes water from a sugar, and breaks down the sugar into complex polymers with a sweet, nutty, or bitter taste and thus produces a golden-brown to dark brown colour?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Caramelisation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Caramelization **is a **process **of **browning of sugar **used **extensively **in cooking for the **resulting sweet **nutty flavor and **brown colour**.
 
• **The brown colors **are produced by **three groups **of **polymers**: **caramelans**, **caramelens**, and **caramelins**.
 
• **Caramelization **is related to the **Maillard reaction**, where **proteins **in **meat turn brown **when **heated **and like the **Maillard reaction**, caramelization is a type of **non-enzymatic browning**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The process of **gelatinisation **occurs when **starch granules **are **heated in a liquid**, causing **them to swell **and **burst**, which results in the **liquid thickening.**
 
• **Dextrinization **is a **special type **of **acid hydrolysis **that occurs by **heating acidified starch **with **reduced moisture **or **heating **of the **aqueous starch **slurry with or **without pH change**.
 
• **The Maillard reaction **is a **chemical reaction **between **amino acids **and **reducing sugars **that gives **browned food **its **distinctive flavor**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct regarding mixtures?

options.text: Colloids are heterogeneous mixtures in which the particle size is large.
The major component of a solution is called the solvent.
The minor component of a solution is called the solute.
A solution is a homogeneous mixture of two or more substances

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Colloids are heterogeneous mixtures in which the particle size is large **__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A mixture is a combination of two or more substances that are not chemically bonded to each other.
 
• Mixtures can be classified into two types: homogeneous and heterogeneous.
 
• Homogeneous mixtures have a uniform composition throughout, whereas heterogeneous mixtures have a non-uniform composition.
 
• The components of a mixture can be separated by physical methods such as filtration, distillation, chromatography, etc.
 
• Filtration is used to separate a solid from a liquid or a gas.
 
• Distillation is used to separate a mixture of two or more liquids with different boiling points.
 
• **Colloids**, also known as colloidal solutions or colloidal systems, are mixtures in which microscopically dispersed insoluble particles of one substance are suspended in another substance. 
 
• The size of the suspended particles in a colloid can range from 1 to 1000 nanometres (10-9 meters) which is **very small**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Solution **

 
• A solution is a homogeneous mixture of two or more substances, where one substance is called the solute and the other is called the solvent.
 
• The solute is the substance that is dissolved in the solvent, whereas the solvent is the substance in which the solute is dissolved.
 
• Solutions can be classified as solid, liquid, or gaseous, depending on the physical state of the solvent.
 
• The concentration of a solution is the amount of solute present in a given amount of solvent or solution.

• The chemical formula **SF6** represents a molecule consisting of one **sulfur (S)** atom and six **fluorine (F)** atoms.
 
• It belongs to the class of compounds known as **hexafluorides**, where six fluorine atoms are bonded to a central atom.
 
• **Sulphur hexafluoride** is widely used as an insulating gas in high-voltage electrical equipment such as **circuit breakers, switchgear, and transformers**.
 
• Its exceptional dielectric properties make it highly effective in preventing electrical discharges.
 
• It is also utilized in the production of **semiconductors** and in various **scientific applications** such as tracer gas studies.
 
• SF6 is considered a **greenhouse gas** with a high global warming potential, and its use is regulated to minimize environmental impact.
 
• The structure of SF6 is **octahedral**, meaning the six fluorine atoms are symmetrically arranged around the central sulfur atom.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **SF2**__
 __
 
• **SF** represents sulphur difluoride, which consists of one sulfur atom bonded to two fluorine atoms. It is different from sulphur hexafluoride.
 
• SF____2 __is not widely used as an insulating gas and does not exhibit the same dielectric properties as SF6.
 
 
 
• __**S6F**__
 
 
• **S6F** is not a valid chemical formula. It does not correspond to any known stable compound and is likely an incorrect representation.

questions.question: Which of the following elements can be used to treat/purify water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Chlorine.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chlorine **elements can be used to treat/purify water.
 
• **Chlorination** is one of many methods that can be used to disinfect water.
 
• It is a chemical disinfection method that uses various types of chlorine or chlorine-containing substances for the oxidation and disinfection of what will be the potable water source.
 
• **Chlorine inactivates a microorganism by damaging its cell membrane. Once the cell membrane is weakened, chlorine can enter the cell and disrupt cell respiration and DNA activity.**
 
• The main objective of this chlorine addition is to disinfect the water and maintain chlorine residuals that will remain in the water as it travels through the distribution system.
 
• Any type of chlorine that is added to water during the treatment process will result in the formation of hypochlorous acid (HOCI) and hypochlorite ions (OCI-), which are the main disinfecting compounds in chlorinated water.
 
• The amount of chlorine that is required to disinfect water is dependent on the impurities in the water that needs to be treated.
 
• Chlorination is able to provide a residual to reduce the chance of pathogen regrowth in water storage tanks or within the water distribution system.
 
• Chlorination has been proven to be very effective against bacteria and viruses.
 
• However, it cannot disinfect all waterborne pathogens. Certain pathogens, namely protozoan cysts, are resistant to the effects of chlorine.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chlorine** was first discovered in** Sweden in 1744.**
 
• At that time, people believed that odors from the water were responsible for transmitting diseases.
 
• Chlorination can be done at any time/point throughout the water treatment process. There is not one specific time when chlorine must be added.

questions.question: Which of the following chemicals are vastly used in the gunpowder of fireworks?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Potassium nitrate, sulphur and charcoal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Gunpowder**

 
 
• It was the** first chemical explosive **and the only one known until the invention of** nitrocellulose, nitroglycerin, smokeless powder, and TNT in the second half of the 19th century.**
 
• Before the invention of gunpowder, many incendiary and burning devices had been used, including Greek fire.
 
• **Roger Bacon invented gunpowder.**
 
• Bacon explored the manufacture of** gunpowder (also known as black powder).**
 
• It consists of a mixture of** sulfur, charcoal, and potassium nitrate (saltpetre).**
 
• Sulfur and charcoal act as fuels while the saltpetre is an oxidizer.
 
• **Bacon **was the **first one in Europe to explain the explosive force of gunpowder.**

questions.question: The synthesis of which chemical is inhibited due to aspirin?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prostaglandins**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aspirin** works by inhibiting the synthesis of prostaglandins, which are chemical compounds responsible for triggering inflammation, swelling, pain, and fever in the body.
 
• It achieves this by irreversibly deactivating the cyclooxygenase (COX) enzyme.
 
• Aspirin, along with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), is highly effective in alleviating skeletal pain, including discomfort associated with conditions like arthritis.
 
• Moreover, aspirin acts as a non-addictive analgesic, meaning it relieves pain without causing dependence.
 
• By impeding the production of prostaglandins, aspirin helps mitigate inflammation in tissues, thereby reducing pain sensations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Prostaglandins **are a class of lipid compounds that exhibit hormone-like properties and are predominantly synthesized by the body at sites of tissue injury or infection.
 
• **Pyrite**, commonly referred to as fool's gold, is a mineral composed of iron and sulfur.
 
• **Histamine** is a chemical present in various cells throughout the body. Its primary role is associated with inducing allergy symptoms, such as nasal congestion, sneezing, and a runny nose.
 
• **Analgesics** are medications utilized for the management and alleviation of pain.

questions.question: Which of the following is an open chain organic compound?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Acetaldehyde**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acetaldehyde** is an open chain organic compound.
 
• An open chain compound, also known as an aliphatic compound, has carbon atoms arranged in a straight or branched chain.
 
• Compounds like **Benzene, Tetrahydrofuran, and Toluene** are examples of cyclic compounds where the carbon atoms form a ring structure.
 
• Acetaldehyde has the chemical formula **CH3CHO** and is a key intermediate in the synthesis of other chemicals.
 
• It is a colorless liquid with a pungent odor and is widely used in the production of acetic acid, perfumes, and flavors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Acetaldehyde** is produced on a large scale in the industry by the oxidation of ethanol or by the hydration of acetylene.
 
• It is an important precursor to several chemicals and is used in the manufacture of plastics, synthetic rubber, and dyes.
 
• Exposure to acetaldehyde can cause irritation of the eyes, skin, and respiratory tract, and it is considered a probable human carcinogen.
 
• Proper handling and safety measures are essential when working with acetaldehyde in industrial settings.

questions.question: Identify the acid that convert zinc into zinc sulphate.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sulphuric acid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In this reaction, Zn metal reacts with dilute H2SO4 to form ZnSO4 and H2 gas is liberated.
 
• Zn is more reactive than hydrogen and hence it displaces hydrogen from dilute Sulphuric acid.
 
• The product zinc sulphate and hydrogen gas is entirely different in chemical properties from the reactant.
 
• Production of hydrogen gas could be seen in the form of bubbles and zinc metal dissolving to form zinc sulphate.
 
• The reaction is found to be slightly exothermic.

Reaction:

Zn + dil.H2SO4 → ZnSO4 + H2 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Sulphuric acid is important in mineral processing, oil refining, wastewater processing, and chemical synthesis.
 
• It has a wide range of applications including in domestic acidic drain cleaners.
 
• It is also known as oil of vitriol.
 
• Dilution of concentration Sulphuric acid is highly exothermic process and hence dilution should always be performed by adding the acid to the water and not by adding water to the acid.
